compareCandidate.label: Area vs. perimeter
compareCandidate.description: Perimeter is the distance AROUND a shape; area is the surface INSIDE it. Two shapes can share a perimeter but have very different areas.

plainLanguageExplanation: Area is the amount of surface a shape covers, measured in square units — little unit squares that tile the shape. For a rectangle, count rows times columns, or just use length × width: a 4-by-3 rectangle covers 12 square units because 4 × 3 = 12. A square is a rectangle with equal sides, so its area is side × side. A triangle covers exactly half of its surrounding rectangle, so its area is ½ × base × height. Area answers 'how much floor, paint, or grass?'

keyFacts.label: Units
keyFacts.value: Square units, like cm² or m²

whyItMatters: Area is how you buy carpet, pour concrete, paint walls, and plant grass. It is the measurement that turns flat shapes into real-world surfaces.
didYouKnow: Area units are ALWAYS squared — square meters, square feet — because you are counting squares of space. The '2' superscript reminds you the measurement covers two dimensions: across and down.
compareReason: Students blur the outline with the surface — comparing around vs. inside makes the two measurements distinct.
